title: Choose Sylph's visual world — fresh hand
question: This hand removes the themed control-room framing and starts from the product, the browser, and the change itself.

options.label: Instrumented Preview
options.lineage: browser inspectors, responsive overlays, and spatial debugging
options.thesis: The running product is the Workspace ground; everything else attaches to what the user and agent can actually see and test.
options.viewport: A persistent left rail groups Repositories and their Workspaces; a live browser canvas owns nearly two-thirds of the remaining screen, a narrow agent thread sits right, and code, diffs, responsive bounds, console evidence, and agent actions anchor directly to the preview as focused lenses.
options.risk: Spatial overlays become noise if more than one inspection layer demands attention at once.

raised.raise: Chrome that carries no action or state is deleted.
Every browser and agent state remains addressable and inspectable in code.
Inactive context recedes through value and depth rather than disappearing.

options.label: Diff Proof Sheet
options.lineage: engineering proof sheets and Diffs-style mixed code views
options.thesis: The change is the interface: intent, edited files, browser evidence, and acceptance read as one continuous proof.
options.viewport: A persistent left rail groups Repositories and Workspaces, opening the selection into one mixed scroll of agent intent, editable file diffs, and large browser evidence, with a persistent live preview strip at the edge.
options.risk: It is the clearest review model but may feel less like a freeform IDE during long exploratory work.

options.label: Layered Workspace
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with acetate leaves
options.thesis: Code, agent context, preview, and tests are readable layers hinged over one shared Workspace board.
options.viewport: A persistent left rail groups Repositories and Workspaces; the live product sits on the base board while a clear active leaf carries code and agent annotations, and a stepped inner tab rail exposes Files, Changes, Preview, Skills, and Runs.
options.case: Layering and tab extent make complex context legible, but the manual voice can imply reference reading rather than live manipulation.
options.risk: Warm paper and tabs can become documentation nostalgia if the preview stops feeling live.

options.label: Change Rail
options.lineage: film cutting benches and perforated select rails
options.thesis: Every agent action, edit, browser step, and test is a frame on one persistent causal rail.
options.viewport: A persistent left rail groups Repositories and Workspaces; a live browser frame dominates the upper field to its right while one precise causal rail crosses below it, keeping edits and agent actions reachable as marked frames.
options.case: Persistent position and visible marks map well to agent work, but a single rail underrepresents simultaneous files and browser state.
options.risk: The orange-and-black commitment can feel editorial rather than comfortably operational over long sessions.

options.label: Typographic Workspace
options.lineage: flat metro tiles and panoramic type
options.thesis: Words, state, and direct surfaces replace most application chrome.
options.viewport: Large pane titles lead into a browser-first horizontal workspace with direct tile entry points.
options.case: Poster-scale type and tiles reduce the density engineering work needs.
options.kept: Delete chrome that carries no action or state.
options.risk: The dramatic type consumes the room needed for code and evidence.

options.label: Addressable Grid
options.thesis: Every Workspace state is a strict code-addressable swap rather than ambient animation.
options.viewport: A tiled Workspace makes browser, code, and agent state explicit at every cell.
options.case: The game grammar misstates the seriousness of ordinary product work.
options.kept: Every browser and agent state remains addressable and inspectable in code.

options.label: Literal Zones
options.thesis: Every zone names exactly what it is and what state it is in.
options.viewport: Literal Workspace, Agent, Code, Browser, and Checks zones make navigation self-explanatory.
options.case: Quotation marks, hazards, and tags become costume faster than system.

options.label: Depth States
options.lineage: cyclorama lighting from night to day
options.thesis: Context recedes and returns through explicit depth phases around the live product.
options.viewport: The browser stays fully lit while code and agent context occupy labeled depth bands around it.
options.case: Light-state transitions do not explain code or causality.
options.kept: Inactive context recedes through value and depth rather than disappearing.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A refined dark agent IDE with a file tree, central editor, chat rail, and browser tab.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional resizable three-pane IDE keeps files left, code and preview center, and agent chat right.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately legible and indistinguishable from the category by design.
